scenes.name: Bud Powell y el piano bop
scenes.author: Ted Gioia
scenes.desc: El piano moderno abandona la densidad orquestal de Tatum y Ellington: mano derecha con líneas rápidas y cromáticas a lo Parker, mano izquierda con escuetos acordes de dos o tres notas, más cerca de Basie que del stride. Bud Powell es el que mejor encarna el espíritu del bebop y el más influyente («si le roban todo, sus pertenencias se convierten en propiedad común»). Protegido de Monk en el Minton's, apaleado por la policía en 1945 y sometido a electrochoques, graba entre 1949 y 1951 sus obras maestras en trío con Max Roach («Tempus Fugit», «Un Poco Loco») y sus Modernists para Blue Note, que anticipan el hard bop. Vive en París desde 1959 cuidado por Francis Paudras (la historia de ’Round Midnight) y muere en 1966. De él vienen Tristano, John Lewis, Hampton Hawes y la escuela de Detroit (Hank Jones, Tommy Flanagan, Barry Harris).

scenes.name: Big bands de repertorio y orquestas contemporáneas
scenes.author: Ted Gioia
scenes.desc: Desde los cincuenta la big band sobrevive como formación ocasional, banda de ciudad o grupo de repertorio. Sauter y Finegan experimentan con instrumentos raros; Don Ellis, Maynard Ferguson y Buddy Rich se acercan al rock y a los compases extraños. La Thad Jones-Mel Lewis Orchestra toca los lunes en el Village Vanguard desde 1966 por diecisiete dólares y sobrevive a sus fundadores como Vanguard Jazz Orchestra. La big band de Toshiko Akiyoshi (pianista a lo Powell, raíces japonesas, diecisiete instrumentos de viento) y Lew Tabackin domina la costa oeste en los setenta. Gil Evans y su heredera Maria Schneider mantienen la devoción por la orquesta; el Smithsonian, el Lincoln Center y las escuelas convierten la big band en pedagogía histórica, como la orquesta sinfónica.

podcast.title: Pioneering Apollo Performance (Pre-1957)
podcast.body: The jazz drummer Buddy Rich is mentioned as possibly having played the Harlem Apollo before The Crickets, preceding them as a white act on that stage. "Bobby Daring had played there before them, and I think so had the jazz drummer Buddy Rich and maybe one or two others."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 74: "It Doesn't Matter Any More" by Buddy Holly

podcast.title: Drum Kit Standardization Efforts
podcast.body: Along with Gene Krupa, Buddy Rich played a crucial role in standardizing how drum kits were constructed and set up. He developed a drum kit configuration that was very similar to Krupa's influential 1948 setup. "Buddy Rich developed something very similar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

podcast.title: Frequent Drum Battle Competitor
podcast.body: Buddy Rich was Gene Krupa's most frequent competitor in popular drum battles, which were held on stage, on television, and on record. These competitions significantly contributed to popularizing drumming. "His most frequent competitor was his friend Buddy Rich."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

xref.title: "World's Fastest Drummer" and Jazz Mentorship
xref.body: Viola Smith earned the moniker "the world's fastest drummer." She further honed her skills by studying and performing with jazz legends such as Buddy Rich and Gene Krupa. She played all over the world before she finally retired from professional life in 1974. "Viola Smith became known as the world's fastest drummer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

xref.title: Big Band Drummer Influences
xref.body: Stephen Perkins' drumming style was heavily influenced by big band drummers such as Buddy Rich and Gene Krupa. This background explains his tendency to play with a "bit of swing," which imparts a looser feel to his overall playing. "His influences were big band drummers like Buddy Rich and Jean Crouppa."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

xref.title: Drum Kit Standardization
xref.body: Alongside Buddy Rich, Gene Krupa made substantial contributions to standardizing the construction and setup of drum kits. By 1948, Krupa's personal drum kit had evolved to a configuration that would be immediately recognizable and playable by any modern drummer. "Also, Crouppa and Rich did a lot to standardize how drum kits were constructed and set up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

xref.title: Early Influences
xref.body: While growing up and playing in local bands, Neil Peart was deeply influenced by prominent drummers across different genres. He admired Keith Moon of The Who, Ginger Baker of Cream, John Bonham of Led Zeppelin, and Mitch Mitchell of The Jimi Hendrix Experience. Additionally, he was fascinated by big band drummers such as Gene Krupa and Buddy Rich. "He loved Keith Moon of the Who, ginger baker of cream, John Bonham of Zeppelin, and Mitch Mitchell of Jimmy Hendrix's groove."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Legendary Drum Battles with Buddy Rich
xref.body: One of Gene Krupa's most popular attractions was the "drum battle," where he would challenge another drummer, most frequently his friend Buddy Rich, to a competition to determine who was superior. These battles were held on stage, televised, and recorded, and played a significant role in making drumming a "really really cool thing." "His most frequent competitor was his friend Buddy Rich."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

xref.title: Punk Rock Accessibility Model
xref.body: Dave Grohl identifies The Ramones as a prime example of punk rock's simplicity and accessibility, noting that their three-chord structure made music seem attainable for aspiring musicians who felt intimidated by virtuoso rock gods. This ease of entry allowed young people to start bands and write about relevant local issues. "And then you hear a Ramones song and it's three chords and you can do that and then you have friends that might not play drums like Buddy Rich or but they can play drums like the guy from the Sex Bistels or because it's so simple, it becomes available to you like, oh cool, well, I could start a band if we do it like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
